- **self**: Salesforce scheduled Case polling versus event subscriptions (15/4)

## How it works

- [statement] Polling clients should retain the timespan of successful replication, cover all relevant changes even when processing overlaps, and resume consecutive timespans after a failed poll. (low confidence) — https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/api/guide/polling-for-changes.html · keywords: Salesforce scheduled Case polling versus event subscriptions
- [statement] Salesforce Pub/Sub Subscribe is a pull-based bidirectional event stream with flow control. Requesting more events on that stream is different from running scheduled record queries. The Node client demonstrates bounded event batches and requesting further batches after processing. (medium confidence) — https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/pub-sub-api/references/methods/subscribe-rpc.html · keywords: Salesforce scheduled Case polling versus event subscriptions · also: https://github.com/pozil/pub-sub-api-node-client
- [statement] Pub/Sub Subscribe uses a long-lived bidirectional stream with pull-based event demand and flow control. An event subscription therefore does not mean repeatedly querying Case records on a schedule, nor does this API use a passive push-only subscriber. (low confidence) — https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/pub-sub-api/references/methods/subscribe-rpc.html · keywords: Salesforce scheduled Case polling versus event subscriptions

## How-to and procedures

- [statement] Use event subscriptions for prompt change ingestion and retain a reconciliation path for Case alert state when missing changes would matter. This is an architectural inference: Salesforce warns that some change events can be lost unrecoverably. Salesforce documents 72-hour event retention; older events can still be available if purging starts later, but storage beyond that period is not guaranteed. (medium confidence) — https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/change-data-capture/guide/cdc-when-to-use.html · keywords: Salesforce scheduled Case polling versus event subscriptions · also: https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/pub-sub-api/guide/event-message-durability.html

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] On a Subscribe error the long-lived connection stops, and the client must retry Subscribe to establish a new connection. (low confidence) — https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/pub-sub-api/references/methods/subscribe-rpc.html · keywords: Salesforce scheduled Case polling versus event subscriptions
- [statement] Salesforce documents a 72-hour retention window for platform and CDC events and does not guarantee retention beyond it. Subscribe replay can catch up retained events, but selecting EARLIEST after a longer disconnection cannot restore events already purged. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-12) — https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/pub-sub-api/guide/event-message-durability.html · keywords: Salesforce scheduled Case polling versus event subscriptions · also: https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/pub-sub-api/references/methods/subscribe-rpc.html
- [statement] A Salesforce support article dated June 5, 2026 says CDC cannot emit a change event merely because a non-persisted calculated value changes; it suggests retrieving unsupported values through scheduled Apex queries or an event-triggered read. Its examples concern UserPresence and AgentWork, so confirm the actual Case fields before applying this limitation. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-06-05) — https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=005224535&language=en_US&type=1 · keywords: Salesforce scheduled Case polling versus event subscriptions

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] A published CDC implementation explicitly uses /data/CaseChangeEvent as a Case subscription channel. Its CometD HTTPS long-polling connection listens for change notifications rather than repeatedly querying Case records; do not confuse this transport with scheduled data polling. (low confidence) — https://datanrg.blogspot.com/2025/06/salesforce-cdc-data-integration.html · keywords: Salesforce scheduled Case polling versus event subscriptions
- [statement] Event subscriptions require recovery state: Pub/Sub clients can store a replay ID and resubscribe within the retained event window. Salesforce documents retention of 72 hours; replay is therefore a bounded recovery mechanism rather than a permanent history. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-12) — https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/pub-sub-api/guide/event-message-durability.html · keywords: Salesforce scheduled Case polling versus event subscriptions · also: https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/pub-sub-api/references/methods/subscribe-rpc.html
- [statement] Salesforce explicitly warns that CDC uses distributed-system semantics: in rare cases event messages are not persisted, are not delivered, and cannot be recovered. Treat event subscriptions as change detection with reconciliation needs rather than an unconditional guarantee that every change is recoverable. (low confidence) — https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/change-data-capture/guide/cdc-when-to-use.html · keywords: Salesforce scheduled Case polling versus event subscriptions
- [statement] For a Case alert whose condition becomes true solely as time passes, plan scheduled evaluation or an explicit timer rather than assuming a new record-change event will arrive. This is a design inference from CDC not tracking changes to non-persisted calculated values and from Salesforce's guidance to query unsupported values on a schedule. (low confidence) — https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=005224535&language=en_US&type=1 · keywords: Salesforce scheduled Case polling versus event subscriptions

## Facts and statements

- [statement] Client applications retrieve changed data by polling periodically. Their polling frequency depends on how quickly changes must appear in the local copy. Salesforce's data-replication guidance recommends polling no more frequently than every five minutes. (low confidence) — https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/api/guide/polling-for-changes.html · keywords: Salesforce scheduled Case polling versus event subscriptions
- [statement] Realtor.com reports that its scheduled Salesforce REST polling risked rate limits and added latency. It replaced polling for Account updates with custom platform events relayed into AWS EventBridge. This is implementation evidence from Account synchronization, not a measured Case-specific latency guarantee. (low confidence) — https://techblog.realtor.com/real-time-account-updates-with-salesforce-platform-events-and-aws/ · keywords: Salesforce scheduled Case polling versus event subscriptions
- [statement] CDC does not remove the need for record retrieval. Salesforce instructs subscribers receiving a gap event to obtain the latest Salesforce record data and reconcile it before resuming normal processing for that record. (low confidence) — https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/change-data-capture/guide/cdc-replication-steps.html · keywords: Salesforce scheduled Case polling versus event subscriptions
- [statement] Scheduled replication polling trades freshness against polling frequency. Salesforce says the interval should follow the business requirement; Realtor.com reports that scheduled REST polling introduced latency and risked rate limits in its Account integration. The Account experience is relevant architectural evidence, not a Case-specific benchmark. (medium confidence) — https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/api/guide/polling-for-changes.html · keywords: Salesforce scheduled Case polling versus event subscriptions · also: https://techblog.realtor.com/real-time-account-updates-with-salesforce-platform-events-and-aws/

## Research summary — Salesforce scheduled Case polling versus event subscriptions

Scheduled polling periodically retrieves Salesforce changes and must manage successful time windows and repeated processing. Event subscriptions expose change notifications through a persistent transport; CometD long-polling and Pub/Sub pull-based streaming are subscription mechanisms, not scheduled Case queries. Implementation experience reports polling latency and API-limit risks. Subscriptions still need replay state, bounded-outage recovery, and record retrieval for reconciliation. Salesforce also warns that rare CDC publication failures cannot be recovered. These distinctions matter when choosing timely Case alert inputs without assuming event delivery replaces all reads.
